title: Infecting human hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells with SARS-CoV-2
author: Huerga Encabo, Ulferts, et al.
materials: EasySep Human Progenitor Cell Enrichment Kit II

steps.title: Verify HSPC source and freshness
steps.instruction: Confirm that a suitable source of human HSPCs (cord blood, bone marrow or peripheral blood) is available; if using fresh material, it must have been collected within the last 24 h, otherwise proceed from step 53 after thawing cryopreserved mononuclear cells.

steps.title: Prepare SARS‑CoV‑2 virus stock
steps.instruction: Produce a defined SARS‑CoV‑2 stock in Vero E6 cells for downstream infections.

substeps.instruction: For each 15 mL of virus stock, seed one 75 cm² flask of Vero E6 cells at ~90 % confluence; set up an additional identical flask for the mock control.
Calculate inoculum volume for an MOI of 0.01 PFU per cell (≈10⁷ cells per flask). A lower MOI may be used at the user’s discretion.
Prepare D2 medium: add (3 mL – inoculum volume) to a 5 mL tube.
Add the calculated inoculum to the D2 medium tube and mix.
Remove existing supernatant from each flask.
Add the diluted inoculum to each infection flask; add 3 mL D3 medium to the mock control flask.
Incubate the flasks for 30 min in the biosafety cabinet, gently redistributing the supernatant repeatedly to keep cells moist.
Discard the supernatant as infectious waste.
Rinse each flask twice with 10 mL D2 medium.
Add 15 mL fresh D2 medium to each flask and place them at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Infect Vero E6 cells and incubate
steps.instruction: Maintain the infected and mock flasks, observing them twice daily from 2 days post‑infection for cytopathic effect (CPE).

substeps.instruction: Use an inverted phase‑contrast microscope to compare infected monolayers with the mock control; no CPE should appear in the mock.
Harvesting before clear CPE yields low titer; harvesting after peak CPE may reduce infectivity.

steps.title: Monitor CPE and harvest virus
steps.instruction: When fulminant CPE is evident, collect supernatants and process them for storage.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the infected‑flask supernatant to a centrifuge tube; dispose of the flask and attached cells as infectious waste.
Transfer the mock‑control supernatant to a separate tube; dispose of its flask and cells similarly.
Centrifuge each tube at 500 g for 10 min at 4 °C to pellet debris.
Aliquot 200–1000 µL of the cleared infected supernatant into screw‑cap tubes (e.g., 200 µL and 500 µL aliquots).
Aliquot 500 µL of the mock supernatant into a screw‑cap tube; discard the remainder.
Store all aliquots at –80 °C. For best infectivity, keep aliquots frozen ≥16 h before further use and avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Process blood or BM sample
steps.instruction: Prepare the primary human sample for mononuclear cell isolation.

substeps.instruction: Place a dedicated disposal bag for all blood‑contact materials.
Turn on the biosafety cabinet, wipe down surfaces, pipettes, and T‑175 flasks with 70 % ethanol.
Estimate total volume of fresh blood or bone marrow aspirate.
If using StemCell Technologies bone marrow (Cat#70001), thaw the sample in pure FBS and centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min at 20 °C before proceeding to step 52.
Dilute the blood/BM 2:1 with PBS (e.g., 150 mL blood + 300 mL PBS). A 3× dilution (150 mL blood + 450 mL PBS) can improve mononuclear‑cell layer clarity.

steps.title: Set up Ficoll gradient and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Separate mononuclear cells using a Ficoll density gradient.

substeps.instruction: Pour the diluted blood/BM into a large tissue‑culture flask and mix with the appropriate PBS volume.
Aliquot 15 mL of Ficoll‑Paque into each 50 mL Falcon tube (prepare enough tubes for 30 mL of diluted blood per tube).
Gently layer 30 mL of the blood‑PBS mixture onto the Ficoll surface, using the lowest pipette speed and a horizontal tube orientation to avoid mixing.
Centrifuge the tubes at 450 g for 30 min at 20–25 °C with the brake OFF. Ensure the centrifuge is at room temperature for correct Ficoll density.

steps.title: Collect and wash mononuclear cells
steps.instruction: Harvest the mononuclear cell (MNC) layer and clean it.

substeps.instruction: After centrifugation, four layers should be visible: bottom red blood cells, Ficoll, a thin middle MNC layer, and top serum.
Using a pipette, carefully collect the MNC layer from each tube and pool into a new 50 mL Falcon tube until you have 20–25 mL total.
Dilute the pooled MNC suspension 1:1 with PBS + 2 % FBS (add an equal volume of PBS + 2 % FBS).
Centrifuge the diluted suspension at 300 g for 5 min at 20 °C.
Discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Lyse residual red blood cells
steps.instruction: Remove remaining erythrocytes using ammonium chloride lysis.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend each cell pellet in 20 mL ammonium chloride solution; combine up to five pellets in the same 20 mL volume.
Incubate at 20–25 °C for 5 min.
Add 2 mL heat‑inactivated pure FBS to buffer the lysis.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min at 20 °C and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend cells and count
steps.instruction: Prepare a final cell suspension for downstream enrichment.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 5 mL 2 % FBS/PBS.
Count viable cells using an appropriate method.
Proceed to HSPC purification (step 54).

steps.title: Enrich HSPCs with EasySep kit
steps.instruction: Isolate human progenitor cells using magnetic negative selection.

substeps.instruction: Adjust the mononuclear cell suspension to 5 × 10⁷ cells/mL in 5 mL polystyrene tubes (maximum volume 2 mL per tube).
Add 50 µL per mL of EasySep Enrichment Cocktail; incubate 15 min at 20–25 °C.
Add 100 µL per mL of EasySep Magnetic Particles; incubate 5 min at 20–25 °C.
Top up each tube to 2.5 mL with 2 % FBS/PBS, place tubes in the magnet, and incubate 10 min at 20–25 °C to capture lineage‑positive cells.
Transfer the non‑magnetic (enriched) cell suspension to a new 5 mL polystyrene tube.
Centrifuge the transferred suspension at 300 g for 5 min at 20 °C.

steps.title: Stain cells for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Label enriched cells with antibodies and viability dye for FACS sorting.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the antibody cocktail as listed in the key resources table; make a master mix by multiplying each reagent volume by (N + 1), where N = number of samples.
Protect antibody vials from light (turn off hood lights).
Centrifuge the enriched cell pellet (from step 54e) for 5 min at 300 g, 20 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in the appropriate volume of antibody cocktail (flow buffer = 2 % FBS in PBS).
Incubate at 4 °C for 30–60 min, covering tubes with aluminum foil to prevent photobleaching.
Wash cells by adding flow buffer at ≥10‑fold the staining volume (e.g., ≥1 mL for 100 µL staining) and centrifuge 5 min at 300 g, 20 °C.
Prepare DAPI viability solution: dilute DAPI 1:1000 in flow buffer.
Discard supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in the DAPI solution.
Filter the suspension through a cell strainer to remove clumps that could block the sorter.

steps.title: Prepare collection tubes for FACS
steps.instruction: Set up tubes to receive sorted populations.

substeps.instruction: Label four 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes for the intended populations (e.g., HSCs, ERP‑S1, ERP‑S2, ERP‑S3).
Add 200 µL pure FBS to each tube (PBS + 2 % FBS may be used, but pure FBS gives higher recovery).

steps.title: Sort, centrifuge, and resuspend sorted cells
steps.instruction: Collect, concentrate, and place sorted cells into culture medium.

substeps.instruction: Perform fluorescence‑activated cell sorting using the gating strategy shown in Figure 3, depositing cells into the prepared FBS tubes.
After sorting, centrifuge each population at 300 g for 5 min at 20 °C.
Resuspend the cell pellet in StemSpan SFEM supplemented with 100 ng/mL each of rhFLT‑3L, rhSCF, and rhTPO (e.g., 5 000 cells in 400 µL in a 48‑well plate).

description:
CRITICAL: SARS-CoV-2 and any material that has been in contact with the virus should be handled and disposed of in accordance with your local regulations.
CRITICAL: Institutional permission to manipulate human samples should be approved before starting the protocol. Ensure you have availability of a suitable source of HSPCs (i.e., cord blood, bone marrow or peripheral blood). In the case of processing fresh samples you should be processing a sample that has been acquired within the last 24 h. In the case of processing cryopreserved mononuclear cell suspension you should proceed from step 53 for the isolation of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) populations. The isolation of primary human stem and progenitor hematopoietic cells under sterile conditions has been optimized in this protocol using FACSAria III in a CL2 cabinet.A
